Round 4151.decision_summary: The policy reply-auto-timestamp (G5 of the switch catalogue): what a queryable's reply carries when its handler gave it no timestamp. Upstream's reply builder holds only the time its caller gives (reply.rs, default None) and stamps puts alone (session.rs, new_timestamp); a node that wants its replies ordered by one clock had no way to say so. Off is upstream's. On, QueryResponder stamps its four plain reply forms (reply, keyed, delete, keyed delete) with the next stamp of a ReplyClock, which NodeHlc is, so a reply and a put of one node are ordered by one clock. A reply with its own time, an error, and the forms that are unstamped on purpose keep none. The host gives the clock to a queryable only when the policy is on and the queryable stamps.

Round 4160.decision_summary: The carry item "the drop counters of TlsListener are not reachable from the C ABI" is paid, and not with a new door. A C program has no listener handle, so an accessor would have had to be a process-wide count behind a new wz_ext symbol; the node already has a log that the library writes what it says about itself into (event-ring, library sources from 0xFF00), and a handshake the arena or the key store had no room for is what the node should say there. The host provider now keeps the typed listener (TlsDial::listen_counted) and, in a build with event-ring, writes one library event per drop: source 0xFF01, level 255, two integers, why (stalled, no room, other) and the channel's own code. Measured on the way: an arena that runs out is the channel's OutOfMemory, in the handshake with the RSA configuration and in starting the session without it (accept answers that one with an error, which TlsListener now counts as well); a key store with no free slot returns PSA's insufficient-memory code, which the channel maps to the same, read and not measured. The meaning of last_drop changed to the latest drop's own error, None for a stall, so that an event can say what it was. The zenoh-c ABI's header does not list the source: that ABI has no secure channel on this engine.

Round 4165.decision_summary: The capability declarations-synced-event (G3 of the switch catalogue). A listener saw the peer's declarations as a stream with no mark where the peer's picture of itself ends and live changes begin, so a program could not read "no subscriber on this key" as "nobody wants it". The boundary is one wire message, the DeclareFinal of the initial interest, which ends the first burst of subscribers, queryables and tokens alike; so it is a fact of the peer, not of a plane. DeclEvent::Synced is delivered to a listener of any plane, once per establishment, by the host session reading the subscriber plane's flag before and after a dispatch. A listener declared after the peer finished is not told, because it was not given what came before: it reads Session::peer_declarations_final. Off, nothing is installed or fired.

Round 4169.decision_summary: The carry item "a key store with no free slot is read to map to the channel's out-of-memory and was not measured" is paid, and the reading was wrong. A new test binary (wz-tls-mbedtls tests/key_store_exhaustion.rs) starts an arena of 64 MiB so that the key store of the host build (1024 keys, four per held session) runs out before the arena does: 255 sessions are held, the 256th handshake is dropped and counted, and the arena's peak is 5.0 MB of the 64 MiB. The channel's error for that drop is Code(-0x6E00), Mbed TLS's generic handshake failure (MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE), not OutOfMemory: Mbed TLS reports the PSA refusal from inside the handshake under its own code, so the channel never sees PSA's insufficient-memory code on that path. The code alone therefore does not name a full store (a refused peer gives the same one); the held count and the arena's peak do. The event log follows: NO_ROOM is the arena's, and a full key store is reported as OTHER with that code. The words in stream.rs, wz-capi-coop tls.rs, events.rs, event_log.rs, wz_ext.h and the design note that said the arena or the key store had no room for NO_ROOM were corrected to say the arena only. Round 4172.decision_summary: The capability remote-declaration-watch (G3 of the switch catalogue). A declaration listener is told what the peer declares, and a session is one link, so the peer is whoever the session is connected to; that holds only while the listener never outlives the link. A session that reconnects can meet another peer, and a callback that reads the session's peer in its own time cannot order the reading against the event. So the identity travels with the event: it is read when the event is staged, in the dispatch that carries it, and the deferred callback receives it as data. Every DeclEvent now carries the peer's zenoh id (DeclEvent::peer), including Synced. Off, the field holds None and nothing of the session is captured or read.

The listener-constructing impl block now names the bound SessionLinkActions: Send + Sync + 'static, which the concrete runtime meets. scripts/lib/feature_gate_diagnostic.py decides the feature as gating no public path. docs/remote-declaration-watch.md. Tests: the existing listener tests carry the new field; a pair, one with the capability on (each event of a named peer carries that peer, and a second peer is named as the second) and one with it off (the session knows the peer and the events say nothing of it).

Round 4176.decision_summary: The rows of the five fixed-memory images that the kit lane and Layer Qzk hold are repaid for the SCE pin 9619440966, which regenerated the codecs and moved no row. The chains, the bounds, the text totals and the owners that moved past their tolerance (the session core, the codecs, the forge runtime, the session mcu) are committed; the stack of the plain, batching and heap clients is 4,608 bytes, of the asking client 9,792 and of the admin image 13,824, each a quarter free over the figure it is sized from; the line of the contract's entropy-draw rule moved from 6184 to 6228 with the session actions that grew above it. The kit then read the stack in a run: 3,416 bytes for the plain, batching and heap clients, 8,360 for the asking client, 4,304 for the secure-channel client and 7,744 for the admin image. The first three are 24 over the bound 3,392 and the asking client 1,020 over its bound 7,340, which the resource gate calls a hole in the model and refuses as a row; the rows therefore keep their earlier readings with the finding written in each, the secure-channel client's reading (4,304) is committed, and the stacks of the plain, batching and heap clients are sized to the reading. What the model misses is not found: the reading rose by 696 bytes (and by 4,144 for the asking client) where the bound rose by 36 (and by 3,008). The frame of 3,696 bytes is the thing to find first.

Round 4178.decision_summary: The stack bound model is mended where the kit's reading exceeded it, and the entry before this one is corrected: its rows kept readings under the old bound and called the excess a hole to find. The kit's debugger found it. A data watchpoint on the main stack, below the depth the bound allowed, halted the plain client in the encoder at the end of its worst chain, and a dump of the stack with the frame-pointer chain showed three things the model left out. (1) The 72 bytes beneath wz_app_main: the kernel's z_thread_entry, bg_thread_main and the app's main (56 bytes) and 16 of thread-local storage and alignment at the top of the stack; the contract now names them (thread_entry) and the bound adds them, the frames read from the image. (2) A function that allocates a word with a store below sp and write-back (str.w fp, [sp, #-4]!, the compiler's alignment after an odd push) was four bytes short in the frame reader, which counted only pushes and subtractions; it counts that word now. (3) For the asking client, the closure of send_get_parts, a frame of 3,328 bytes under the dispatch of the events, was not among the callees of the contract's tx-encoder rule, so the bound never followed the GET's own send, and the same watchpoint found it as the function that wrote 1,020 bytes past the bound. With these the bounds read 3,472 bytes for the plain, batching and heap clients and 9,344 for the asking client, above the kit's readings of 3,416 and 8,360; the chains read 2,656, 6,888 and (the admin image) 9,632; the stacks are 4,672, 12,480 and 13,888, each a quarter free over the bound. The rows hold the kit's readings of the SCE pin 9619440966 (3,416 for the three clients, 8,360 for the asking client, with chain_misses back on the asking row because its reading is again over its direct chain), their notes say what was found, and the six images, built and run on the kit, hold every static gate and their rows. The two frames of the asking client (3,696 and 3,328 bytes) remain the thing to find and remove.

The dissector test that held the usrpwd body walker to this tree's own method moved with the method, and now reads the OpenSyn the core's encode_open writes around a body a real handshake through two dispatches produced, with the responder's acceptance of that very extension as its control; the core keeps its hand-laid body tests. Round 4187.decision_summary: A consumer claim, forwarded by a peer session: a throughput view draws payload bytes per keyexpr and per step, and the census gives the size only as capture totals per keyexpr. Sizing an entry from its payload slot (end - start, shm_descriptor) would be a second size rule, and it disagrees with the census exactly where the census cannot measure: a query value's slot includes the length prefix, and a value whose encoding the walk cannot read has no slot and a census answer. So every carried entry now carries payload_size, the census's own answer for the message the session parsed at the entry's place: classify's size reading is split into one read_record that the census counts and payload_size reports. A key of its own beside payload, null where the census sizes nothing. Fields 55.

What the node carries in this stage is its id (z_info_zid, z_session_id), z_close, z_session_is_closed and the drop, which closes a node first since dropping a node does not stop it. A client told no router still scouts for one and is refused by the key; a build without the feature refuses every custom south as before. Round 4191.decision_summary: The third pool of the host's listing is the runtime's task table. Its cells are what a session's task takes after the session slot and the pump cell, and a node whose tasks ran out refused a dial or an admission without the document saying which table was full. The table answers as a pool: its cells, those that hold a task or a result nobody has read, the most that held one at once (a mark noted when a cell is taken, zero-sized when the build keeps none), and the spawns that found no free cell. A task too large for a cell stays a count of its own and is not a want of room, so it is not in the pool's refusals. The MCU session host, and the lwIP host that wraps it, list session-slots, pump-cells and task-cells in that order.

Round 4198.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI holds a node, stage two: put, delete and the subscriber. A node opened through wz-capi-c now publishes and subscribes. z_put and z_delete publish through the node's data plane (RouterForwarder::publish_with) by the text of the key, since a node names every key whole on the wire, and a payload in shared memory goes out as its bytes until the node carries the descriptor; the codec's refusal is the one the registry reports, a message too large to send. z_declare_subscriber hosts the subscription on the node (host_subscriber_from), and the subscription holds the data plane counted (RouterState::shared_forwarder) so that z_undeclare_subscriber withdraws it after the session handle has been let go of. The state behind a z_owned_subscriber_t is now a holder, the registry's SubId or the node's hosted id, and the entity id reads the session identity from the holder. The test opens a node that partitions its south and a registry peer that dials it and requires what each puts to reach the other's subscriber; it fails with the node's put disabled (the peer never hears the node) and with the node's subscriber disabled (the node never hears the peer), each alone. Operations not yet carried still answer Z_EUNAVAILABLE on a node, now checked with the timestamp of a session's clock.

Round 4203.decision_summary: The fourth pool of a node's listing is the listener's lanes, and the listing gains the means to hold more than one owner. The lanes are not the session host's: the listener is declared apart and the host never holds it, so a host's listing could not say them. The listener answers as a pool (lanes, those that belong to a session, the most that did at once where the build keeps a mark, and the InitSyns dropped for want of a lane alone, since an InitSyn that another table refused after the lane was taken is that table's) and lists itself as listener-lanes. PoolList is implemented for a reference to an owner and for a pair of owners, so a node writes one document for (&host, &listener) without a collection and without an allocator.

Round 4206.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI holds a node, stage three: the publisher. A publisher declared through a node's session handle is now a publisher of the node: the handle slot of a z_owned_publisher_t holds a PublisherHandle, the registry's PublisherState or a NodePublisher that keeps the key, the options its puts start from and the node's data plane counted, so that it can be used and dropped after the session handle has been let go of. z_publisher_put and z_publisher_delete publish through that data plane by the text of the key (the same node_publish the session-level put uses), z_publisher_keyexpr and z_publisher_id answer from the handle, and z_undeclare_publisher drops it. The matching of a publisher (its status and its listeners) is the matching family and answers Z_EUNAVAILABLE on a node through one helper, not_a_registry_publisher, in place of the Z_ENULL of a handle that is not there. The identity a NodePublisher keeps is read only by z_publisher_id, which the build without the unstable API does not have, so it is held under that cfg; a peer session found the same dead field in the subscriber (landing apart). The test declares a publisher on a node that partitions its south, requires a registry peer that dials it to hear what the publisher puts, a delete to go out, the key and an id of the node's session to be answered and the matching status to be unavailable; it fails with the publisher's put disabled.

Clippy with router-node and the unstable API off fails on the dead zid of the subscriber in sub.rs, which a peer session found at the same time and is landing apart; it names nothing of the publisher, whose identity is held under the same cfg, but that configuration is not shown clean here until that landing. Three runs failed on the way and were fixed: a test import used only with router-node, and one run started from the wrong directory (not a code verdict). Not run: the other wz-capi-c tests, the footprint and size gates, a node's put of shared memory, Layer Z, Z8.
carry_forward_bullets: Stage four of the C ABI node: get, the queryable and the querier, then liveliness and the matching of publishers and queriers (the publisher declares no interest on a node yet, which the matching needs), then shared memory, the advanced pair, the group, the info peers and routers, the transport and link events, the declared key expressions and the timestamp. A node opened through the C ABI answers Z_EUNAVAILABLE to those. The build with router-node and without the unstable API has to be shown clean once the subscriber's dead field is landed by the peer session. A put of a payload in shared memory goes out as bytes on a node. A C ABI router that keeps no south is still the registry of faces, which forwards nothing; opening every router as the node is a parity decision of its own. Whether router-node belongs in a Kconfig switch and a footprint budget is not decided. A client that is told no router and keeps a south is refused even when it scouts nothing. The dialled-subregion cases are witnessed in process only; no stock zenohd witness. Round 4210.decision_summary: The first step of the stream link for a node with no heap (the switch link-tcp for the cooperative engine) is the framing, moved before anything is built on it. A length-prefixed stream is cut into frames by one state machine, the window, which the host's registered-slot reader already ran. A node's receive callback needs the same decisions (the prefix width read when a prefix starts, a zero-length batch skipped, an untrusted four-byte prefix refused before anything is carried, a frame lying whole in one read lent and not copied), and two copies would let a link mean one thing on a host and another on a node. The window now lives in wz-session-core, unconditional and without an allocator, over a Carry that holds the frames which span reads: a Vec on the host, FixedCarry on a node, where a spanning frame larger than the carry is refused with its length and a whole frame of any size is still passed. The host keeps its names, so the ring reader is untouched.
changes_bullets: wz-session-core stream_window.rs (new, unconditional): prefix_width, decode_prefix, MAX_FRAME_PAYLOAD, WindowError (OversizeBatch, CarryTooSmall), the Carry trait with impls for Vec and FixedCarry, and RxWindow over a carry, with tests of every chunking of a wire over a heap and a fixed carry, the lent and the assembled frame, the oversize prefix, a fixed carry refusing only a spanning frame larger than itself, the end-of-stream question and a width change mid-prefix. wz-runtime-tokio: link_rx_window names the machine as RxWindow over a Vec and re-exports WindowError and decode_prefix, its implementation removed, and the differential test against the sized reader is kept; prefix_width forwards to the core.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the seven stream_window tests of wz-session-core pass, the four link_rx_window tests of wz-runtime-tokio pass (among them the every-chunking test that holds the window to the sized reader), and clippy with warnings denied is clean for both crates (the only warnings are the vendored ring crate's). The framing refusal reachability gate, the prose-name gate, the armed-oracle census and the feature surface census pass; no feature or CONFIG name was added. The ring reader (runtime-tokio-uring) was not built: it uses RxWindow::new and push through the unchanged alias and matches no WindowError variant.
carry_forward_bullets: Only the framing is moved. The node's TCP link still needs the lwIP TCP sources in the build (the stack is built without TCP), a peer address that carries the protocol in place of the UDP peer, a driver for a stream that holds a send slot until a partial write completes, the closed driver enum that lets one host mix UDP and TCP, the capability link-tcp with its Kconfig, and the probe of a node keeping a session with a stock router over tcp/ for 2000 requests and reconnecting. The window is not yet fed by the stream reader of the standalone engine on the host; the wide legs with the ring reader were not run.

Round 4212.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI holds a node, stage four a: get and the queryable. A session opened as a node now asks and answers. z_get on a node's handle goes through RouterState::get as the node's own face: the router routes it to the queryables of every face that holds one on the key and to its own, each reply is handed to the same reply gate and C closure the registry's legs use, and the C drop(context) runs when the node lets go of the leg's callback. A get that brings a cancellation token is refused by name with Z_EUNAVAILABLE: the token stops the legs a registry fans out and a node has none to stop yet. A query value in shared memory goes out as its bytes. z_declare_queryable on a node hosts the queryable on the data plane (host_queryable_from), and the state behind a z_owned_queryable_t is a holder, the registry's QblId or the node's hosted id with the data plane counted, so that the queryable can be withdrawn after the session handle has been let go of. The marshal of a query is generalised over what it is held through: QueryRoute and HeldRoute are the registry's face or the node's holder, so that an escaped query is answered on the route it arrived on, and the node's concrete holder (RouterQueryHolder, RouterHeld) is public in wz-capi-core so that the C ABI names no port trait. router-node now implies query and queryable, whose code the node arms are in. The test has the node answer a registry peer's get and the peer answer the node's get (the node's own queryable let go first, since it answered its own get at the first try); it fails with the node's get disabled and with the node's queryable not hosted, each alone. The querier is the next part of the family (4b).

Round 4213.decision_summary: The second step of the stream link for a node with no heap: lwIP's TCP is in the library when asked for. The stack was built without TCP, its port headers fixing LWIP_TCP at 0 and the source list leaving the TCP files out. The choice is now one feature of lwip-sys, tcp: with it build.rs compiles tcp.c, tcp_in.c and tcp_out.c, defines LWIP_TCP=1 for every translation unit (the sources, the shim and bindgen alike) and binds the raw API the stream link uses; the port headers leave TCP off unless it is defined, so the feature is the one place that decides for the host port and for a deploy-supplied one. Without it the library and the bindings are the UDP-only ones, as before. A test drives a connection over the loopback netif through the raw API with the explicit poll of a NO_SYS node: listen, accept, connect, send, receive, acknowledge the receive window, and close from both ends.

The tests of the crate take a gate and initialise lwIP once (a second lwip_init asserts, and lwIP is not thread-safe), and the new TCP test runs a loopback connection both ways with a close from each end.
verification_bullets: On a build host: the tests of lwip-sys pass with the tcp feature (the loopback connection and the existing smoke test, run together under the gate) and without it, and clippy with warnings denied is clean with it on. The feature surface census, the feature gate diagnostic and wz_config --check pass. The cross build of lwip-sys with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em against the cross-test port was started and stopped by the system for low memory before it built anything, so it is NOT run; the headers' change is neutral with the feature off (the cross builds of the images do not set it), and Layer Q is not re-run for that reason.

The session handle holds the node counted (SessionHandle::Node is an Arc of RouterState) so that a querier can ask after the session handle has been let go of; a get on a node that was closed with its session answers Z_ESESSION_CLOSED and is not left waiting for an answer that cannot come. z_querier_get issues the get through the same issue_get_on_node the session-level z_get uses, so the reply gate and the refusal of a cancellation token are one; z_querier_keyexpr, z_querier_id and z_undeclare_querier read the handle. The matching of a querier (its status and its listeners) is the matching family and answers Z_EUNAVAILABLE on a node through one helper, not_a_registry_querier, as the publisher's does. The test has a node declare a querier and a registry peer's queryable answer its gets, requires the querier's key and an id of the node's session and the unavailable matching status; it fails with the node querier's get disabled.

Round 4216.decision_summary: The third step of the stream link for a node with no heap: one TCP connection of lwIP's raw API as a byte stream a cooperative loop can write to and read from without blocking (wz-link-lwip, feature tcp, LwipTcpSocket). Its state is address-stable storage lwIP's callbacks write into, a heap box or with static-link-storage a cell of a static pool (TcpSocketPool), written in place because it holds the receive buffer. The receive buffer is the flow control: a byte is acknowledged and the window reopened when the application reads it, so a buffer at least the port's window (read from the port through a shim, TCP_WND) holds anything that can arrive, and a smaller one is refused at connect. A write queues all its parts or none; a part lwIP then fails to queue would leave half a frame in a stream, so the connection is aborted and the call says so. The shim reads two lwIP macros Rust cannot reach, the send buffer left and the window.

verification_bullets: On a build host: the six tcp tests of wz-link-lwip pass (0.01 s), and clippy with warnings denied is clean with tcp and with tcp plus static-link-storage. The feature surface census, the prose-name gate, the armed-oracle census and wz_config --check pass. Two earlier runs of the same tests did not finish: the wrap test waited without a bound for echoed bytes the server had dropped, and both runs were cancelled after hours; the test now sends in lockstep and every wait is bounded. The feature gate diagnostic was not re-run (wz-link-lwip is off its axis) and the cross build of lwip-sys with tcp for the MCU targets is still not run; Layer Q is not re-run because the images do not set the feature.
carry_forward_bullets: No listener: a node accepts no TCP connection yet, only dials. The socket is not the cooperative engine's StreamSocket: that trait blocks in send and wait, and an adapter over this socket for the lwIP node (the wait polls lwIP, local and peer addresses read through the shim, the dial returning when the handshake completes) is the next step, then the peer address and the closed driver enum that let one host mix UDP and TCP, the capability link-tcp with its Kconfig, and the probe against a stock router. The receive window is lwIP's default (four segments of 536 bytes), so a stream moves about 2 KB per round trip; its limits are not the stream link's yet. The cross build with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em against the cross-test port is still not run; Zephyr's port keeps LWIP_TCP at 0.

Round 4217.decision_summary: The fourth step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the stream link the cooperative engine already has, written once for every stack with sockets, now runs over lwIP. The engine's StreamSocket and StreamDial are blocking contracts (a write returns when the stack has taken every byte, a wait when bytes are queued or the time is out), and lwIP here runs NO_SYS on the one thread that drives the session, so nothing moves in it until it is polled. LwipTcpStream and LwipTcpDial therefore make each wait a loop that polls lwIP, its input path and its timers (the acknowledgements and retransmission that move a connection), until the thing waited for has happened or the time is out. The time is the port's own millisecond clock, read through a shim, so the host and a deploy each keep their own definition. A dial returns when the handshake completes and is refused on a reset or after five seconds; a table without room is Exhausted, and a receive buffer below the window is Unsupported.

The feature surface census and the prose-name gate pass. Not run: the cross build of lwip-sys with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em (still, since the system stopped it for memory), the static-link-storage form of the tests (it is compiled and linted, not run: the tests use a heap box and the engine's heap transmit store), and Layer Q (the images set no tcp feature, and the new shim function wz_lwip_now_ms is not referenced by them, so the linker drops it; a footprint row that moves says otherwise).

Round 4218.decision_summary: The stream link of the cooperative engine cuts a stream into batches in its own buffer, in place, while wz-session-core now holds a window that cuts the bytes a reader was handed. The first carry of the stream link said the driver should take the window in its place. That was wrong: the driver reads into the tail of one linear buffer and lends each batch where it lies, with no second buffer and no copy, which is the design a node with little memory wants, and the window would add a carry and a copy. So the two stay two designs for two kinds of reader, and the rule they share is held by a test instead: however the stream is cut into reads (every pair of cuts of a wire carrying a plain batch, an empty one, a one-byte one and a longer one), the driver and the window hand over the same batches, and both pass the empty batch over.

Round 4219.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI holds a node, stage six: the matching of publishers and queriers. A publisher or a querier declared on a node now reports what matches its key. The node's publisher and querier hold the node counted (NodePublisher and NodeQuerier keep an Arc of RouterState in place of the data plane alone) and declare an interest on its data plane, which the node's router answers with the declarations beyond it, and withdraw it when they drop. z_publisher_get_matching_status and z_querier_get_matching_status read RouterState::matching_status (the subscribers for a publisher, the queryables for a querier, only the complete ones when its target is ALL_COMPLETE, as the registry's reads them); the owned and the background matching listeners of a publisher and the owned one of a querier are watches of the node's own face (RouterState::watch_matching), ended by the listener's drop. What a matching listener is declared on is now one type, MatchTarget, the registry's MatchId or the node's watch with the node counted, held by the background hold and by the owned listener alike. The accessors that answered Z_EUNAVAILABLE for these operations have no reader left and are removed. The test has a registry peer hold a subscriber and a queryable on a key and requires the node's publisher and querier on that key to say that something matches, by status and by owned and background listener, and a node publisher on a key nothing subscribes to to say it does not; it fails, each alone, with the publisher's status always false, the querier's status always false, the publisher's owned listener, the querier's owned listener and the publisher's background listener handed nothing.

Round 4220.decision_summary: The fifth step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the accept side. A node listens on a port and takes the connections that arrive on it, each handed out as the same LwipTcpSocket a dial yields, so a session over a connection is the same whichever end opened it. The listener is a static the image declares, as the datagram listener is, with a queue of Q connections waiting to be taken. A connection that arrives with no room for it, because the queue is full or on static-link-storage every cell of the pool is taken, is refused in the accept callback: lwIP abandons it, nothing is allocated instead and the refusal is counted. The connection is registered in the accept callback itself, before lwIP goes on to the data of the same segment, so nothing a peer sent with its handshake is missed. A shim reads the other end's address and port, so an accepted socket knows its peer, which a dialled one learned from its own call.

The first run of the refusal test failed on an assumption about when lwIP tells a refused dialler (it waited for an established state that came or did not, as lwIP chose); the test now asserts only that the dialler ends failed. The accepted connection reaches no session yet: the adapter that makes it a StreamListen of the engine's stream link, the slot stack that dials and accepts tcp/ in a host, the link-tcp capability with its Kconfig, and the probe of a node against a stock router are the steps after. The refusal is lwIP's abandon, without a reset of its own; how soon the dialler learns of it was observed to vary and is not asserted. The MCU cross build with tcp is still not run.

Round 4221.decision_summary: The sixth step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the accept side meets the engine. LwipTcpListen is the engine's StreamListen over the static listener of the link tier, so a node takes the connections that arrive on its port as the same LwipTcpStream a dial yields, and the stream link over a connection has nothing to tell which end opened it. Each accept polls lwIP once, because a connection arrives as its handshake is processed, and wraps the oldest waiting connection with its peer read from the socket. One test holds the whole path together: a dialled end and an accepted end, each under the engine's stream driver, carry a 300-byte batch one way and a 500-byte batch the other, whole, with the accepted end knowing the dialler's port.

Round 4222.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node: the first of the carried debts, the cancellation token of a get. A get on a node is now ended by the token it was made with, and a liveliness get on a node takes the token as a registry's does. The node's own face learns to end a query it holds: a new command CancelQuery(rid) delivers the one final the held query waits for (LocalLiveliness::cancel_query), RouterState gets get_numbered, which answers the request id the query was asked under, and cancel_get(id), which ends it; RouterState::get keeps its signature. issue_get_on_node registers the token's fan before it asks, as a registry's get does (a token whose cancel has started fails the get with Z_EGENERIC), and records, after the id is known, the undo that cancels the query on the node; a token cancelled while the query was being asked runs the undo there and then. The cancel of the token waits for the registrations to be released, which the face does as it lets go of the query's handlers, so the closure's drop(context) has run when the cancel returns. A liveliness get on a node takes its snapshot on the face's thread before it returns, so there is no leg to stop; the token is registered for its length and one whose cancel has begun fails it with Z_EGENERIC. The refusals by name (Z_EUNAVAILABLE) that stage four and five left for a token are gone. The test has a registry peer's queryable hold a query for four seconds, the node's get be made with a token, and the cancel return at once with the get's closure let go; it fails with the cancellation not registered (the cancel then waits the query out, 3.95 s).

Round 4223.decision_summary: The seventh step of the stream link for a node with no heap: the pieces meet the engine's slot stack. The engine already has IpStack, one stack for udp/, tcp/ and tls/ links that claims each link's buffers from the image's byte tables and yields the one driver type the session host runs, with an acceptor for the connections of a listener. It was written over a datagram socket the platform provides, which lwIP's UDP is not, so a node of tcp/ links names a datagram socket that does not exist: NoDatagram, as the stream side has NoStream and NoDial, with a DatagramSocket::CARRIED constant the stack asks before it claims anything. A udp/ dial on such a node is then Unsupported and permanent, never an Exhausted that is retried. LwipTcpStack is that stack over lwIP's dial. A test dials and accepts through it, shows the udp/ dial refused with every table still empty, and carries a batch each way between the two drivers.

Clippy with warnings denied is clean for wz-session-lwip and wz-runtime-coop with tcp, session-slot and session-unicast-accept, and for wz-session-lwip with tcp. Not run: the cross build with tcp for thumbv7m and thumbv7em, Layer Q, and the static-link-storage form of the tests.

The node that listens and dials (the admin node of the slot profile) is typed to the UDP driver and is not made generic; a node of tcp/ links is built from the generic session host and the connect manager until it is. Mixing udp/ and tcp/ in one host needs lwIP's UDP to be the engine's datagram socket, or a closed driver of the two; neither is done. The link-tcp capability with its Kconfig, a listener close, the probe against a stock router and the MCU cross build remain.

Round 4224.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node: the second of the carried debts, the payload of a put in shared memory. A put (z_put and z_publisher_put) made on a node with a payload that is a chunk of shared memory now goes out as the chunk: RouterState::publish_shm with the chunk's send handle, which the node sends as its descriptor to a face that negotiated shared memory and as its bytes to any other, as the registry's put does. node_publish_payload is the one place a node's put decides which of the two a payload is. The value of a query is not carried the same way: RouterState::get takes bytes and has no descriptor path, the Rust API's node asks with the bytes as well, so a get on a node sends a chunk-valued query as its bytes and that stays. The test puts a chunk through a node to a registry peer that dials it and requires the peer's subscriber to be handed the payload as a chunk of shared memory (z_bytes_as_loaned_shm answers Z_OK); the same test run before the change reached the peer and failed on its being the bytes of the put, so the two are a pair.

Round 4225.decision_summary: The eighth step of the stream link for a node with no heap, and the first that runs a session over it: one node dials a tcp/ endpoint and another takes the connection off its listener, each on the session host of the fixed-memory profile over the stack of the step before, and the handshake runs through lwIP's TCP, the engine's stream link and the slot tables. Both ends reach the established state, the dialling link takes a receive buffer and a frame buffer from the image's tables and the accepted one a receive buffer from its own, and when the dialler closes the acceptor's session ends. The two nodes share one program, one lwIP stack and one cooperative thread, as the UDP exhaustion tests run theirs; what the test holds is that the pieces fit, which the drivers' own tests could not say. No source changed: the stack, the dial, the listener and the host were enough as they were.

Round 4227.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node: the third of the carried debts, the meaning of a C ABI router. In a build with router-node a router opened through the C ABI is now the router data plane whatever it holds, where it was the registry of faces unless it kept a south apart, and the registry joins none of the faces it holds, so a router that was one forwarded nothing between its clients; mode "router" asks for a router, and a router that forwards nothing is a preset that does not do what upstream's does. OpenPlan::node_role names the node a role is opened as for a surface that opens every router as one (a router always, a peer or a client by node_for_south, as before) and the C ABI's open reads it; the Rust API opened every router as the node already. A peer or a client that keeps no south apart is still the registry of faces in the C ABI, which is the same question for a peer that listens and is left as it was. A build without router-node is unchanged: its router is the registry of faces, which forwards nothing, and that is now written in the carry. The test has a router and two clients that dial it and cannot reach each other, and requires what one puts to reach the other's subscriber, which only a router that forwards delivers; run against the open as it was before this change it failed on the put never reaching the other client, so the change turns it. The older routers tests of the file still pass, a router that listens on nothing hears its own put.

Round 4228.decision_summary: Where the stream link of a node with no heap stands before the switch that selects it. The engine's admin node, AcceptingAdminNode, is already stack-neutral: it takes the host, a binder, an acceptor of the links a peer opened and the factory, and the Zephyr secure-channel admin node is that node. A node of tcp/ links over lwIP is therefore that node over the stack of the earlier step and needs no node code, only a Copy stack, because the node holds it as its host's and a copy as its binder. LwipTcpDial, and so LwipTcpStack, are Copy when the link handle is. The capability link-tcp and its Kconfig are NOT declared in this round, for two reasons: the MCU's Kconfig axes belong to the zephyr-admin-node image, whose lwIP backend builds only the UDP node, so an option would select nothing that builds (and the declaration declares no option that cannot be built); and on the host the tcp/ link is in every build, so a switch needs the tcp code gated and every combination built.

Round 4234.decision_summary: A consumer claim, forwarded by a peer session, the second half of the one round 4193 answered: the consumer still spelled the selector term from a node itself, a second copy of the grammar, and nothing proved a node's term selects its own row. So the library writes the sentence (filter, add to the typed selector, exclude from it) from the node object, and a node whose value is lost gets the reason. Its soundness is one oracle for the tests and a fuzz target: every node of every record answers its sentence yes, every sentence a document offers is one a record of that row proved, the row fold is read under a greedy cover, and the exclusion is the sentence's negation. Held over every seed capture and codec noise, the oracle found eleven places where the selector read a row otherwise than the field document shows it, each in the planes or the document rather than in the sentences, and each is fixed at its cause rather than excused in the oracle. A path once published is kept: an append-only registry, renames that resolve a former name, and the field list naming them.
changes_bullets: wz-capture: selector_term writes a node's sentence (term_for, read_node, term_json), the term being the shortest tail of the path that names the field and no other; a scouting root is unjudged, a null path unnamed, a lost value unwritable. doc_revision adds selector_term revision 1 and selector_fields revision 5 (renamed).

wz-capture: selector_term::soundness is the property as one oracle: the record level over every record's tree as the planes build it, the bridge holding each offered sentence to what a record of that row (flow, direction, anchor) proved, the row fold read under a greedy set cover, violations counted by class with examples, and a record or row the oracle cannot read reported rather than passed over.

wz-capture: a row's key is its list, direction and produced-index (payload RowKey), so two rows of one datagram list no longer share one; the fold contract feeds the row, and the request index keeps only where held rows begin.

wz-capture: field_path builds the declared shape once (field_path/shape.rs), indexed by last segment; a record tree carries the tree beside it (the Fragment a joined record was completed in, a paired close's own message), the part of a batch past either reader's stop is read as an unread record inside its transport message (Envelope::Remainder, RowFacts::unread_remainder), an empty batch as its transport message, and a record the walker reads otherwise than the session is the one the row shows.

wz-capture: the row plane judges a row the codec could not decode, by its MID and its walked tree; the field document walks a datagram row in the space the session read it in and writes a packet anchor under packet; a zid path compares the zero id.

Round 4235.decision_summary: A defect found reading the code for the board image, in the stream the earlier steps built: its blocking waits (a dial's handshake, a write's wait for send-buffer room, a read, an accept) poll lwIP's loopback queue and timers, and an Ethernet interface's frames reach lwIP only when its MAC is polled, which is the image's. The host tests ran over the loopback, which lwIP moves by itself, and passed; on a board the SYN-ACK of a dial arrives through the MAC, so every dial would have waited its five seconds and been refused. The image now says what else a poll does with a Service, a plain function so the dial, the listener adapter, the stream and the stack stay Copy, and each poll runs it first, as the node's own loop pumps its ports before lwIP's timers. A dial or listener given none polls as before. A test counts the service across a dial, a wait and a read.

Round 4252.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven begins with the two operations that need only the session's id: the stamp of a timestamp and a declared key. z_timestamp_new on a node mints the same word the registry mints, the wall clock through wall_clock_ntp64 and the zid of the session that stamped it, which the node has as the registry does. z_declare_keyexpr on a node returns the key it names with no alias bound, because a node names every key whole on the wire (a put by a declared key already goes out by its text on the node), and z_undeclare_keyexpr on a node has no alias to retract and consumes the value as it does on the registry. Both used to answer Z_EUNAVAILABLE on a node. What stays unavailable is stated in the doc and in a test that probes it: the routers and peers of a session, the transport and link events, the resource snapshot, the shared-memory provider, the advanced publisher and subscriber, the group.

Round 4258.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: what the faces of a node say. The peers and routers a session is linked to (z_info_peers_zid, z_info_routers_zid), the transports and links it lists (z_info_transports, z_info_links) and the listeners that hear of a transport or a link coming and going (the declared and background forms of both) now answer on a node from the node's own face table, where they read the registry's sessions. One value carries it, FaceSource (SessionHandle::face_source): the registry's SharedSession or the node's RouterState, answering the faces it holds, the observer that watches their coming and going and the undoing of it, so a listener keeps its own copy and unwatches after the session handle is gone. The node answers from RouterForwarder::face_snapshots and watch_faces, which the Rust API's node reads the same way, so no core change was needed. A node joins no multicast group through this ABI, so its transports are its unicast faces. The resource snapshot stays unavailable on a node on purpose: it counts the messages a session received, a node counts none, and a snapshot of zero would read as a node that received nothing.

Round 4259.decision_summary: A node declaration could name commanders (decision D12) and the generator wrote their lists into the node's constants, but the declared node bound no verb: nothing in the slot client read the lists, the target's vocabulary still said the commander role was built, and a declaration with a commander had never been packaged (the build's view of it fell over the commander's missing locator). The verbs are now bound where the authority is decided, once: a client of the slot profile that names a commander registers one queryable more, `@/<zid>/client/session/**`, answered by `admin_fixed::VerbLegs` over the store its connect manager holds the nodes in, judged by `Commanders` for the zid the link's key proved, by the same `lifecycle_verdict` the admin node uses. The commander of a verb is the zid of the link the query arrived on, one hop: a router's key when the router forwarded it, the asking node's own only on a session it holds with this node. So that a node can hold such a session, the slot node now has the secure channel's server side (`listen-tls`). The vocabulary says a role is built only when the image's own manifest has the feature that does what the role grants (`role_features`), and the secure_channel condition states the one-hop rule.

Round 4264.decision_summary: The runtime task tables of the fixed-memory node images hold one cell per session, not one more. The tables were declared SESSIONS + 1 "with room beside" the pump tasks, but a node spawns no task besides a session's pump (the only spawn on the slot path is spawn_pump), and a session's cell is held until its handles are let go, which is the moment the session's slot is freed, so the cells in use never outnumber the slots in use. session_pool_exhaustion holds this at the host: it fills the tables to exactly N sessions (the task table of 2N + 1 cells is exactly full at the N + 1th session) and readmits a peer into the cell a closed session freed. The udp, tcp and mps2 node images and the secure-channel loopback witness (both of its nodes) now declare TASKS = SESSIONS. Static RAM falls by one cell: 4,864 bytes in each of the udp (698,908 to 694,044) and tcp (634,204 to 629,340) images, 4,320 bytes of .data in the mps2 image and 9,664 bytes of .bss in the witness.

Round 4265.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: the advanced publisher. The composite (AdvancedPublisherOn, in wz-ext-pubsub) was hosted only on the registry through CPlane, so ze_declare_advanced_publisher answered Z_EUNAVAILABLE on a node. The composite is generic over a plane, so a node gets a plane of its own, NodePlane: the cache queryable is hosted on the node's data plane (host_queryable_from, retracted by unhost_queryable on drop), the @adv liveliness token is the node's own token (declare_token and undeclare_token), a put is the node's publication (publish_with, or publish_shm for a chunk), the heartbeat period is a thread that ends when its timer is dropped, and the entity id comes from a process-wide counter. The clock is the node's: RouterForwarder::node_hlc hands out the node's shared NodeHlc (a second clock with the node's identity would break the uniqueness of its stamps), so a node whose role does not stamp refuses a cache with no miss detection with Z_EGENERIC, as upstream's does. The state of an advanced publisher in advanced.rs became a host (the registry's shared session with its composite, or a node with its composite and the interest it declared on the node's data plane so that a node below a router learns of the subscribers beyond it), and the matching of an advanced publisher (listener, status) reads the host. The registry arm is the code it was, moved under the host. What stays unavailable on a node: the advanced subscriber and its matching and liveliness, the group, the resource snapshot.

Round 4266.decision_summary: Round 4259 bound a declared node's commanders to the verbs, and a consumer could still not write a grant to a declared node: a node with a secure channel made its key when it started, so its zid was known only once it ran, while a grant is compiled into the node that holds it. A declaration may now state the node's identity, `[identity]` with the files of its certificate chain and private key: read at start, not compiled in, because the key is the device's secret and an image is a file that is packaged, hashed and handed around. The key is taken only when its owner alone may read it, its text is wiped once the channel holds it, and a node that cannot be the identity it was told stops rather than make another. The zid it proves is known before it runs: `wz_node.py --zid-of` prints it from the certificate, by the rule the vocabulary states, so no consumer writes the rule again. Running the two nodes found that the declared node's reply line was cut at the console's 256 bytes, so a reply past about a hundred bytes was reported as other bytes than the node kept; the line is now written whole.

Round 4270.decision_summary: A Response read where its frame lies is now read as its view. `lend_response` decoded the codec's lent Response into a binding of its own, a record of over a kilobyte (its extension lists are inline, sized for the deployment's node), where `lend_request` has read a Request as a view of a few words since the asking client's frames were first measured; the same SCE peer that owns the pin measured the generated decode of a lent reply at 304 bytes and its encode at 232, so the frame was the value wz held, not the generated code. Round 4273.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: the advanced subscriber. Its host (EngineSubscriber, in wz-ext-pubsub) is written over the port's SessionEngine and nothing else, and ze_declare_advanced_subscriber read the registry, so a node answered Z_EUNAVAILABLE. A node is now an engine: RouterState implements SessionEngine (a new file in wz-capi-core, drive/router_node/engine.rs), each operation being the one the node's data plane already does for the program that holds it. A subscriber is hosted on the data plane (one callback, where a registry mints one for each face), a liveliness subscriber is the node's own face's, a queryable is hosted with the node's holder, a token is the node's token, a get is the node's own face asking (one leg, whose callback is let go at the query's end, with its cancellation recorded on the fan), matching reads the node's tables, and the faces are the forwarder's; subscribers and liveliness subscribers share the one id space the port states, held by a map. Periodic jobs (the history's and the recovery's periods, the beacon's) run on PeriodicJob, a thread that ticks until it is dropped or its tick says stop; the advanced publisher's heartbeat of the previous round moved onto it, so there is one such job and not two. What a node does not do is stated in the file: a write filter holds nothing back (the router forwards by what the faces declared), the declared keys are none (a node names every key whole on the wire), the batch windows are zenoh-pico's, and the liveliness get is not offered through the engine yet. The state of an advanced subscriber in advanced.rs holds a host (the registry's shared session or the node), which the detection of publishers reads to declare its liveliness subscriber on the node's face, and the node's liveliness field in RouterState became counted, so that the cancellation of a query can hold the face on its own. Round 4278.decision_summary: Item 751 step (b), the C ABI node, stage seven: the group. Unlike the advanced subscriber, the runtime's group (wz-runtime-tokio group.rs) was not written over the port's engine: it is bound to a unicast Session and to tokio tasks, and the C ABI joins one such group for each face the registry holds and takes their union in the aggregate (GroupAggregate). A node is one data plane, not a session, so the owner chose to lift the shared core and not to write a second group: what the two hosts share is now wz-session-core's group_view (the keys, the ids that may join and in what order they are refused, the keep-alive period, GroupEvent, MemberTable and react, which apply an event to the table of known members with their lease deadlines and say what the host must do: tell the user, or ask the member for its record). It is written over plain values with no lock, no clock and no channel, so it is no_std and the runtime's group and the node's both run it. The runtime's Group was moved onto it (its ten tests pass as before; the view of known peers is ordered by member id now, where it was in a hash map's order). A node joins ONE copy over its engine (NodeGroup in wz-capi-core, group/node.rs): the join is announced on the event key before the event subscriber is declared, the subscriber and the member's queryable are hosted on the data plane, the keep-alive and the watchdog are the engine's periodic jobs (no tokio runtime is asked for, which the registry's join needs entered), and a member heard of by its beacon alone is asked for its record by a query of the node's own face, every answer kept; its events go into the same aggregate under one source, so the view, the leader, the events and the wait are the C program's as before. wz_capi_c_group_join reads the handle and holds either host (GroupHost) and leaves it when dropped, the sink retired first as the registry's leave does. A group id or member id that may not join is Z_EINVAL on a node as on the registry, and a refused declaration Z_EGENERIC. What stays unavailable on a node: the resource snapshot.

Round 4282.decision_summary: The multicast session's task (multicast_pump_task, the group node's pump) is written as the session's task is: a function that returns an async block and not an async fn, and spawned with the future made in its cell. As an async fn it held each by-value argument twice in its future, once as given and once as the local its body moved it into (the reason pump_task is a block), and its callbacks carry the node's state (the group's observer, the publisher's schedule); and spawn_multicast_pump built the future by value on the caller's stack before the spawn. The future of the group's task no longer holds those copies, and the spawn no longer needs a frame as large as the future. The function's callbacks are closures, so their types cannot be named from outside the group's join and the cell of the group's task cannot yet be derived as the session's is (cell_bytes_of takes a function of two arguments, and the group's task takes four, three of them closures); that is the next step, not this one.

Round 4285.decision_summary: A participant with an allocator reads a chain of any length. The owned parse (`parse_frame_payload`) decoded each record in the lent form at the NODE's capacity (`wz_codecs::lent`, the lists inline at the deployment's capacity, eight extensions to a chain) and refused the ninth as storage (`CapacityExceeded`), where the protocol bounds a chain by nothing and upstream reads any length: the carry item of round 4167, held as an expected behaviour by a test of its own. The seven records of the owned parse are now read in the lent form at the heap's capacity (`LentHeap`, `Lent<'f, WireStorage>`: the lists grow, the bytes are the frame's, so the shared-bytes origin projection is as before) and then moved into the owned message as they were. The test that held the refusal now holds the acceptance (9, 40, 300 and 5,000 extensions, the payload after the chain the one on the wire, the nested chain of that length), and the best-effort walk's test, which used the ninth extension as its record that halts the walk, uses a record the frame ends inside. A build with no allocator is unchanged: it never had this parse. The same round limits what a test build writes to a disk, after a lane took 90 GB of a build machine's: the dev and test profile keeps the line tables and drops the rest of the debug information (a test executable was 125 MB, now a fifth of that by the usual ratio, to be measured on the next lane), and the nondefault-tests gate deletes the test executables a leg built once the leg has run them (the libraries stay, so a later leg builds only what its features change). Merging each crate's integration test files into one executable, the structural remedy, is a separate piece of work that starts from a measurement.

Round 4291.decision_summary: The structural remedy for the size of a test build is measured and its tools are in. Each of the 584 `tests/*.rs` files of the crates is a test executable of its own that links the whole dependency tree: one feature set of `wz-integration-tests` (317 files, default features only) is 71.3 GB of target on a build host, 318 executables of 217 MB each with the line tables only, and Layer C1bnl's 99 legs took 90 GB of a build machine's disk. Merged as `tests/it` (`tests/it/main.rs` with the files as modules under `files::`), the same crate is 4.9 GB (minus 93 percent), 4 executables, and builds in 89 s where it built in 133 s on the same host, with the same 999 test names (`merge_tests.py --compare`) and every test passing (lib 60, `it` 38 with 798 ignored, `it_zenoh_pico_sys` 93, `it_wz_capi_pico` 11 ignored). Three facts the measurement found and the tool now holds: `zenoh_pico_sys` (the vendored C library) and `wz_capi_pico` (its drop-in) define the same `z_*` symbols, so one executable cannot link both and a file that uses one goes to a target of its own (`it_<crate>`); a file that installs a `#[global_allocator]` or has a `[[test]]` table stays its own executable (35 and the tables of six crates); and a file that runs its own binary by test name (`current_exe` with `--exact`) must name the test by its module path, which two files of this crate now do by `module_path!()` so that the name is right in both layouts. The move itself is not in this round: more than twenty gates read `crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/*.rs` by path and `run-ci.sh` names the files 230 times by `--test`, so the move carries them, and this round holds back until they can see both layouts. This round lands what is independent of the move: `scripts/lib/merge_tests.py` (plan, apply, compare, selftest), `scripts/lib/test_build_size.sh` (the measurement, from a fresh target), the two files that name a child test by its path, and the repair of a red another session's test file left on main: `bounded::census::no_test_runs_a_child_with_a_bare_output` read the helper `Node::output` of `wz_declared_commander_zenohd_interop.rs` as a bare `.output()` of a child, so it is `console` now.

Round 4294.decision_summary: A declared node's identity can now be made on the device it runs on. The node binary takes `--make-identity <certificate> <private_key>`: it generates a P-256 key in PSA with export allowed, signs a self-signed certificate over it, and writes the key (SEC1 DER armoured as PEM, created 0600 with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW and fsynced) before the certificate beside it, then prints the certificate's PEM on stdout. Nothing is ever overwritten: when both files are there it reads them as the node would and prints the certificate that is there; when only one is there it makes nothing and says so, so that a key is never paired with a certificate that is not its own; a certificate that fails to write takes its key back. The key's DER and PEM are wiped once written. The vocabulary's identity entry names the command and states that it never overwrites, and the zenohd interop test now provisions both nodes with the node's own maker instead of the external tool, holding that the printed certificate equals the file, that the key is 0600, that a second run changes nothing, that half an identity is refused, and that each node proves the zid --zid-of names for its certificate.

Round 4295.decision_summary: Phase 1 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md: a face's runtime is kept apart from the routing facts the tables hold about it. The session's actions, the messages held for the face's link, the waker of its gate and the numbers of the declarations sent to it are not a version of the tables: the data path writes each under a lock of the face's own while it holds the read guard, and a face has one of each whichever version of the tables routed a message to it. They now live in one FaceRuntime per face, which RouterFaceState holds as an Arc, so that a later copy of the tables (phase 3) shares a face's runtime instead of duplicating it. Under structure A nothing moves: no change of logic, of the order of sends, or of which lock is taken where.

Round 4297.decision_summary: Phase 2 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md: a route memo keeps the newest inputs it has served. A route is a function of the graph and the interest table, kept by the versions of both (RouteInputs) and served only at the inputs it was computed at. Until now a store or a refresh at any other inputs cleared the memo; once readers hold different versions of the tables at once (structure B), a reader of an older version would clear what a reader of a newer one stored, a loss of work and never of correctness. RouteInputs::precedes orders inputs: both members are counters a write of the tables moves forward and nothing moves back, living as long as the hat that owns the memo (verified: the tables and their memos are constructed together, and the counters are sums of Versioned counters). A store from inputs that precede the kept ones returns its route and keeps nothing; a refresh to them moves nothing and asks the table nothing, decided under the read lock. A pair where neither precedes the other (a wrapped counter) replaces the memo, as every move did before, so the cache cannot be held back by an unordered pair. Under structure A inputs never go back, so nothing changes there.

Round 4303.decision_summary: Phase 3 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md: the router's tables are Clone by path copying at field granularity, so that the snapshot cell of phase 4 can publish a new version by copying only what a write reaches. Each hat's graph and interest tables, each face's routing facts, and the keyed stores beside them sit behind an Arc, and a writer reaches each through a named accessor that calls Arc::make_mut, which copies only when another version shares the component. The route memos are shared by every version and never copied (phase 2 made that sound), and each face's runtime stays shared as phase 1 left it. The recompute flag of a mesh hat and the record of the tokens advertised into each region lose their locks: every write of both was traced to a writer of the tables (the methods that write the record now take &mut self under T: DerefMut, so a reader cannot reach them by type), and the record sits behind an Arc like the other stores. Nothing clones the tables yet outside a test, so under structure A every Arc has one owner, make_mut never copies, and no behaviour moves.

Round 4304.decision_summary:
Two hosted reds are repaid at their root. The nightly Fuzz run (42016507903, at b0caa2b649) failed its `selector_term` job on an input from the `pcap` corpus. The soundness oracle offered the term `Push.del.timestamp.zid == 617320737570726f63205d393420205b` and found it Unknown over the very record whose tree held the field (rule S1). The input was a `Frame` whose `Push` carried a `Del` with a timestamp of a twenty-byte zid. The generated timestamp codec refuses that zid (`sce:max-size="16"`), and so do zenoh-pico and zenoh. The dissection walker read any VLE length, and every reader of a zid field reads at most sixteen bytes, so the zid printed as a value that did not name its own bytes. The walker now refuses a zid past sixteen bytes in `SpanCursor::zid`, the one constructor every zid site goes through. Two of those seven sites take a VLE count (the timestamp and the linkstate entry); the other five take a four-bit nibble and could not exceed it. The refusal is the codec's own `LengthOutOfRange`, and the dissection's serde name table now names it, so a persisted dissection records it by its name and not as "Unrecognised".

CI run 42011089802 (at 0c7298a48d) failed Layer C1cn: clippy `large_enum_variant` on `wz-zenoh`'s `Engine`. Its `Router` variant was at least 352 bytes, against 104 for `Tokio`, once the router node took an ABI extension and an engine state of its own (8ef208ab60, ed4d766806). The variant is now `Box<RouterEngine>`. A node is opened once, so one allocation keeps every peer and client session at its own size. The session that owns the router mode of `wz-zenoh` was told before the fix.

The same run's other two reds were attributed rather than repaired here. The bare-`.output()` census red in `validate + verify + test` was already repaid by 3522f080a1. The C1cs red is the eight cases that round 4290 and 9e3e643439 moved. That run predates both, and its hosted readings all fall under the moved budgets: pico-client 1,892,417 against 1,906,600, pico-default 4,470,378 against 4,499,900, capic-default 9,606,825 against 9,642,000. The fleet measurement 4290 rested on therefore agrees with the hosted machine.

Round 4311.decision_summary: Phase 4 of docs/router-table-snapshots.md: the router's tables can be shared as published snapshots, value `snapshot` of the new choice policy `routing-table-sharing`, beside `rwlock`, upstream's reader-writer lock, which stays the default and the value of every upstream preset. One cell (router_forward/tables_cell.rs) holds the tables in either form behind the seam the router already had (OnTables over a read or a write). Under `snapshot` a reader loads the last published version from an ArcSwap and pins it for its thread, so that every nested read of that thread routes by the version its outermost read loaded, as a thread's reads see one state under the lock; a writer takes the writers' mutex, drafts the next version as a path copy of the published one (phase 3), and WrittenTables::drop, the one commit point, publishes the draft with one store before letting the mutex go, or abandons it when the write unwound. The guarantee that nothing is sent to a face after it left is held under `snapshot` by a grace period: deregister, after its write is published and the mutex released, waits until no reader holds a version retired before it, and a thread that holds a version and asks for a grace period is refused by an assertion, since it would wait for itself. The multicast ingress now owes its callbacks to the end of the route as the unicast paths do, under both values, so a callback of the node's own subscriber may declare while the group's ingress routes to it. The draft is allocated as the Arc it is published as, so a publish moves nothing. What `snapshot` gives up is stated in the policy's help: a message routed under the version before a change may reach a link after a declaration that change sends to the same link, which no rule of the protocol orders. Nothing here says what either value costs; phase 5 measures both against the baseline of round 4286. The same land counts the router tests of phases 2 to 4 in the CI lanes that pin them (C1AY, C1X), whose counts phases 2 and 3 had left behind.

Round 4314.decision_summary: The steps for what only a stream suffers (a connection that ends by FIN or by RST, one that falls silent, a listener that stops, a message the network cuts or joins, a peer that comes back) are designed by the property a stream link owes and built on an instrument that makes the network do each, and the instrument is the first piece. scripts/lib/stream_fault.py is a TCP proxy with one control for each thing a network does (close_all, reset_all, blackhole, refuse, segment, and hold with flush), and it is deterministic by construction: a counter is raised before the bytes it counts are sent, every thread waits on events (select and a wake pipe) and none decides by a timer, the thread that owns a resource carries a control out and acknowledges it so a control returns when its effect is in place and the connections the kernel had established before it are taken first, segmentation is judged by the writes the proxy made and a merge is an explicit barrier, an orderly release is the half-close protocol so unread data never turns it into a RST, and the cases wait on a signalled state and never sleep and look. A first version of the same proxy flaked in 3 runs of 30, from a counter raised after the send and from a close that raced the thread using the socket; the design above is what removed those causes and not a longer wait. HARDWARE_VERDICT.md states the properties, the rules the steps follow (a fault on one leg observed through another, bounds from the node's contract and not from a run, a step that waits for a state and not for time) and the reference-model discipline the steps are accepted by.

verification_bullets: The proxy's selftest holds each control to its effect as the ends see it, against a real echo server on the loopback (EOF with no reset for an orderly release even with 20,000 bytes in flight, a reset for an abortive one, silence with nothing forwarded and the bytes counted dropped for a black hole, a refused connect and a held connection that still works for a closed listener, the proxy's own write log for segmentation, one write for a hold released by a flush). It passes 300 runs in one process, and 100 runs beside 64 busy processes on a 32 core machine, with no failure; the earlier version failed 3 of 30 and, before that, 4 of 6. The selftest bites: with the count made after the send it fails three cases at once, and with an abortive release made orderly it fails the case that holds it. gate_provenance_lint, round_fed_gate_reach, the board table gate and the verdict program's selftest pass, bash -n and shellcheck are clean. carry_forward_bullets: The stream steps are the next pieces, in this order: the reference model of the contract with a fault of the model for each way a node breaks a property (a cell lost on a reset, a FIN ignored until the lease, a re-dial with no wait, a silent peer never detected, an accept queue that sticks); the steps for release, conservation and re-establishment, with the fault on one leg and the observation through the other (router B gets a REST port, and the node's second endpoint is reached through a proxy); the selftest's drift check that holds the program's copy of the retry schedule, the lease and the cell count equal to the node's source; then silence, framing and admission, QEMU first and the kit after. The node's behaviour under these faults is not known: a step that finds a node breaking its contract is a defect to repair at its root, and is the point of the steps.

Round 4324.decision_summary: The first steps for what only a stream suffers are built: HW.36 (an orderly release by the peer ends that peer's session and no other, at once), HW.37 (an abortive release: the same) and HW.38 (conservation and re-establishment: after more releases than the node has cells the node still takes its peer back and holds one session for it). A step is a stimulus, an observation on the other leg and a comparison that is a pure function of what was observed. The comparison is the only thing that decides: the wait runs to a hang guard and measures, and judge_release and judge_conservation judge, so weakening a comparison goes green and no second term holds the step red. The bounds come from the node's contract and not from a run: the lease the node advertises, the keep-alives in it, the retry schedule of a dial and the cells of its pool, held equal to the node's source by a drift check that names the constant that moved. Prompt means below the earliest moment a lease could have expired (the lease less one keep-alive interval, three quarters of it), so a node that waits out its lease fails. The acceptance of the steps is a reference model of the contract on a virtual clock with a fault for each way a node breaks a property: each model fault reds exactly the step that holds its property and no other. A first real run against the node under QEMU read the node's own console as 2, 1, 2 sessions three times while the program saw no release: a router redialling at once passes the one-session state before the next read. A state that holds is the observation, so each release now closes the leg to new connections before the fault (the counter before the effect) and opens it after the read, and the model implements the refusal.

Round 4325.decision_summary: The silence property of a stream link is the fourth step of the stream suite: HW.39, a peer that falls silent with its connection open is detected by the lease, only its session ends, and the peer is taken back. Its window is derived from the node's contract and not read off a run: no sooner than the lease less one keep-alive interval (a node that drops a quiet peer earlier breaks the lease, because the last keep-alive it heard was at most one interval before) and no later than the lease and one interval. The fault needed the proxy to change first. A black hole dropped the bytes of both ends but still passed on an end's close, and router A has a lease of its own that runs out at about the same moment as the node's, so its close would have reached the node and the step could not have told the node's lease from the router's. The black hole now swallows an end's close (the pump counts it, then waits on the proxy's condition, with no timer) and delivers it when the black hole ends; an abort wakes a parked pump. The step holds the leg closed to new connections for the measurement, so the only way the node can lose A is its own lease, ends the black hole when the node has been read whatever happened, opens the leg, and awaits the peer's return. The comparison is one pure function, and the reference model has two more faults: a silent peer held for ever, and a quiet peer dropped after a second.

Round 4326.decision_summary: The re-establishment property of a node that dials is the fifth step of the stream suite: HW.40, the node re-dials a lost peer on upstream's schedule of waits (1, 2, 4 and 4 seconds, read from the policy in the node's source) and a new outage restarts it. The wait is not read by polling the node's status: a remaining wait read at a poll depends on the poll's cadence. A second proxy sits on the leg the node dials B over, the node is told to dial it, and the proxy stamps every connection it takes on its own clock before it does anything with it, so the gaps between the node's dials are events. The proxy gained reject: while on, a connection is taken from the listener and reset at once, so a dial reaches a listener and fails (unlike refuse, which closes the listener and leaves the dials unseen), and the control is applied by the accept thread and returns when it has. The step loses B's session with every dial rejected and reads four gaps (the loss to the first dial, then dial to dial), each from its wait to the wait and 500 ms (the node drives its dials from a 100 ms tick, so it never dials early and may dial a few ticks late; 100 ms is allowed before the wait for the host's clock against the node's at the loss), lets the dials through and awaits the peer, then loses it a second time and reads the first gap alone, which is the first wait again when an outage restarts the schedule and the ceiling when it does not. The comparison is one pure function and the model has four faults: a re-dial with no wait, a schedule that never grows, one that a new outage does not restart, and a node that never dials again.

Round 4329.decision_summary: The framing property of a stream link is the sixth step of the stream suite: HW.41, a message is read whole whatever the segmentation, shown with every write on the leg to A cut to one byte. The cut applies to the connection that exists and to the one the peer makes next, so the step releases A's connection with the leg closed to new ones, opens the leg and awaits the peer's return: its handshake (Init and Open and their acknowledgements) crosses the leg a byte at a time and the node must read each message whole across as many reads as the bytes arrive in. It then asks through router A, which crosses the cut leg in both directions (a request to the node and its reply), and the answer must list both sessions. Whether the cut landed is not assumed: the step reads the proxy's own log of what it wrote and requires at least 20 one-byte writes each way (a handshake alone makes more), so a run in which the cut never took effect fails by name instead of showing the node whole messages and calling that a pass. The comparison is one pure function; the model has a node that does not read a message that arrives in pieces and a cut that never lands, and the comparison weakened to ignore the count lets the second go green.
