Round 4457.decision_summary: A consumer measured the selection since door of a live handle at 230 to 580 ms a call even when no row had arrived: every call folded the three planes that decide a row's word (payload, exchange and row plane) over the whole capture, then read every row to write the few after the cursor. The planes are folds in capture order, as the census's are, so they are now kept between calls per selector (as many selectors as the handle keeps memories for) and fed only the messages that arrived, going on across a front trim as the field document's pairing does. A row's word is final when its message is taken, except a request's, which is decided when its exchange closes or is displaced; so a call that asks again from the cursor the last document gave reads the rows that arrived and the request rows of the exchanges that were open, and compares only those against the words remembered. Rows are enumerated from per-list marks with the capture order's own continuation, so the document is written in the order a whole enumeration writes it. Whatever can move every row (the grouping, a flow's word a selector reads, a zid prefix, the list ids a `flow` term reads, the planes outgrowing the lists) begins the planes again, and a cursor below the last one or a row with no number reads every row; the header lists these for the consumer. The row plane is now kept in the census's verdict column, since it is now held between calls. A word given while a message was held is not taken back when a ceiling takes the message, so under a trimming ceiling the since door's words can differ from the selection door's, which judges only what is held; the header says so.

Round 4461.decision_summary: The consumer remeasured the selection since door after round 4457: one call fell from 50 to 3 ms at the median and from 492 to 16 ms at the 99th percentile, but under a ceiling that trims the front the 99th percentile stayed out of its budget. The kept planes went on across front trims and kept the verdicts of every row the ceiling took, and past four entries per held message they were begun again over what was held: about once in 30,000 rows on the live tap's ceilings, that call costing the whole walk, and the restarted planes read a final whose request the ceiling had taken as an orphan. The planes key every per-row entry by the row's list and produced-index, and nothing asks for a row its list no longer holds (a document writes only held rows, and a row is asked again only while held), so the entries of rows below each list's first held row are now given up instead: in one pass, when the entries have doubled since the last pass or passed the four-per-held-message bound. The planes are begun again only when what they keep that is not a row's (the exchanges still open) alone passes that bound. The same run found round 4460's red: the dissector now emits `whatami_name` on the Init and Join cbyte, a word read from the `whatami` bits, and the transport layout's closed table refused it as unclassified in 22 tests. A reading is not a field a caller can write, so the table gains a closed list of readings, each naming the bit-field it reads, skipped only beside a row of that field; the round's author agreed.

The range of an integer field is now judged once, in `proto_range`, from the field's protobuf type and the nanopb `int_size` in force (file, then message, then field, merged by the one merger in `proto_nanopb`; a map entry by the file's options alone), as nanopb's generator maps it: a signed varint type to `intN_t`, an unsigned one to `uintN_t`, the fixed widths untouched. The description document (`proto_message` revision 5) gives every field row `value_range` (`low`, `high`, `source`: `type`, or `nanopb_int_size` only when the option narrowed it) or `value_range_refusal` (`not_an_integer`, `enum`, `map`, `unmodelled_option`), and the value door and the end-to-end wrap door refuse a value outside the same range, naming the option. The consumer's comment conventions for value lists and scales are not read: they are not the `.proto` language, and a reader of them would make wz a second owner of a convention it does not define. A caller's choice to send an out-of-range value on purpose was not built; the consumer said it needs none yet.

Round 4463.decision_summary: The memory matrix's two fragment-chain cases went red with round 4452 and further with 4454, for two defects. First, the report left a structure out: the chains that ended without closing (4454) were a deque of 120-byte entries beside the list's chain facts, and `ListMemory::chains` did not count it, so the dissection held 122,880 bytes per doubling of that deque that it did not report. Second, a fragment row's chain fact (4452) grew from a 32-byte map slot (outcome and identity) to a 104-byte one: the fragment's sequence number and length, which its frame carries; its place in the chain twice over (index and offset, and the same two again as what the chain held before it, with the previous sequence number); and, on an abort, what the chain had staged, which is a fact of the chain and was also kept in its ended entry. Both are now kept as the repository keeps rare and per-row facts elsewhere, as packed columns (`column_log`, as the index entries are since round D10). A row keeps its produced-index, its outcome with its reason, its chain's identity (as the count of identities minted and the distance back from the newest, since two conduits' chains interleave and an identity alone does not rise), and its index and offset; its sequence number and length are read off the row's frame by `MessageList::chain_of`, which now takes it, and what an aborted chain had staged is read off the chain's ended entry, found by the produced-index its rows end below. An ended chain is one row of eight columns (rows end, identity, a word that packs the key, the ending, its reason and the head's flags and MID, staged fragments and bytes, first and last sequence number, the head's key id), and the suffix of the key its head names, when it has one, sits beside them by entry number. The report counts every structure: the two column logs, the suffixes with their slots, and both folds (open chains with the suffix each head owns, each key's boundary, ended chains not yet handed on). `ChainFact::before` is gone: on a staged row its index and offset already say what the chain held before it, and only an abort reads it, as `held_at_abort`. Every fact the field document writes (revisions 62 and 63) is read from the same values as before, so no document byte moves. No ceiling moved. Two defects found on the way are repaid here: the chain-sequence fixtures wrote a fragment's sequence number as one raw byte, a VLE only below 128 and wrapped at 256, so past 64 chains half the chains of a run never closed and the matrix measured a mixture its table did not name (now written as a VLE); and the session core's reassembly tests named `alloc`, which a build with `reassembly` and without `alloc` does not link, so that build's test target did not compile (they now take `Vec` from `std`, which a test always links).

Round 4465.decision_summary: The newest hosted run (the last head, run 42755847834) lost its main job at the system-package step: the index refresh succeeded, and the install it led to failed with a not-found for one version of perl that the index named and the mirrors did not hold, every alternate mirror answering ignore. Nothing in the tree was involved, and apt's own last line says what to do. The wrapper every package step of the workflows goes through now tries an install that apt refused once more, after a fresh index refresh and a short pause, up to two attempts in all; a second refusal fails the step by name as the first would have, so no package is quietly absent. An install killed by its deadline is never tried again, because a retry of a silence doubles the silence the deadline exists to bound. The attempts and the pause are environment settings of the wrapper, and the test layer of the wrapper drives three more arms: refused once then taken (the step passes, and the calls are an update, an install, an update, an install), refused every time (the step fails after exactly the two attempts), and hung (the step fails after one install).
changes_bullets: scripts/lib/apt-install.sh: the install loop, the code of the last bounded command kept for the caller, the two new settings and their note. scripts/run-ci.sh: the layer of the wrapper pauses for zero seconds in the arm that expected one refused install to fail, and gains the three arms above.
verification_bullets: The wrapper's test layer, cut out of the CI script and run as one function with its helper on this machine (it installs nothing, it drives stand-ins): it passed with the three new arms in place. As a control, the script before the change was given the same stand-in that refuses the first install and takes the second, and it failed (exit 1) where the changed script passed (exit 0). shellcheck of the wrapper printed nothing. Whether the real mirror race clears within one retry is not measured here.

Round 4466.decision_summary: The liveliness token and the liveliness subscriber can state a set of links, from the registry, the Rust API and the C library. Round 4467.decision_summary: The selector language gains four fixed fields that read the end-to-end judge's verdict on a record: `e2e`, `e2e.crc`, `e2e.counter` and `e2e.timeout`, each with a closed set of words. Before this round the verdict was written only into the field document's `e2e` block, so a reader who wanted the frames whose CRC failed had to open every row; `e2e` as a selector word was refused as an unknown field. (1) The words are made in one place, `e2e_words::E2eWords::of`, from the judge's outcome, and each restates a fact of the block: `e2e.crc` is `crc_error` (`ok`, `error`), `e2e.counter` is `counter_reason` (`none`, `repeat`, `out_of_range`) or `unjudged`, `e2e.timeout` is `timeout_error` (`ok`, `error`) or `unjudged`, and `e2e` is all three (`ok`, `error`, `unjudged`, `none`). Not judged is not failed: the counter of a slot's first frame and of a frame whose CRC did not match, every part but the CRC for a sender the capture never named, and the timeout of a frame whose packet carried no time read `unjudged`, never `error`, so `e2e == error` is the selector for failures and the first frame of every stream is not among them. A payload shorter than the profile's header is `error` (damage); one that is not a run of bytes this reader holds is `unjudged`. (2) A record that carries no frame (a key no profile rule covers, a del, a query, a reply, a request) reads `e2e == none`, decided on every plane with no declarations needed, and carries no part: `e2e.crc == ok` is `no` over it, `!=` is `yes`, as a path the walked tree lacks answers. Whether a published sample is a frame is undecidable only where the judge could not be asked: a door handed no declarations, and a sample whose key did not resolve. (3) A frame's verdict depends on the frames of its slot before it, so the payload plane judges: handed declarations and a selector that names an `e2e` term, it judges every published sample as it walks the capture, in capture order, with the same profile, slot and counter judge the block is written from (`e2e_plane`). The rules are copied into the fold (`JudgingRules`), because a fold is kept between calls and the declarations are text of one call; the rule a key falls to is found by the function the declarations themselves now use (`formats::first_covering`, `first_segment_covering`), so the copy cannot give a key to another rule. A segment rule's piece is read first, as the field document reads it: a piece that completes its message hands the joined message to the judge, and one that completes none carries no frame. (4) A payload plane handed declarations now reads a reference the wire does not answer under the key they fix for its id, as the field document's rows and the values door already do; before, a field document handed `#%id=key` lines printed the fixed key on a row whose `key` term the selector could not decide. (5) The field documents, which take declarations, decide the `e2e` terms. The selection doors, the selected-packets door and the census doors take none, so over them every `e2e` term on a published sample is undecided and never `no`; a selection door that takes declarations is the next round. The selector field list (revision 6) and the selector verdict (revision 10) carry the four fields, and the C header's language table states them.

Round 4469.decision_summary: The hosted CI run of c0455d6f22 (round 4468) ended cancelled: 51 of its 52 jobs passed, and the isolated-crate lanes job was stopped by its 30-minute limit one second after its last lane, Layer C1bf, passed (903 s). Two causes. First, its cache entry had grown to 1,295 MB against a class budget of 840 MB, and the cache pruner's over-target pass dropped it (run 42857288356, `least dear first`), so the next run built cold, and a cold run of this job does not fit 30 minutes; the run that cold build saved is dropped the same way whenever the repository passes its target, so the loop repeats. Second, Layer C1bf clippies wz-runtime-tokio at `--all-features`, which turns on its `rocksdb` feature, and the job never restored the native RocksDB engine that `.github/actions/rocksdb-engine` keeps in a protected cache, so every cold run compiled RocksDB from source inside the clippy step. The rule the earlier splits followed (round 4245 for the analyzer crates, round 4359 for their docs) is to split rather than raise: a larger limit is spent by the next lane the genre gains. The three wz-runtime-tokio matrices (C4c, C4d, C1bf) therefore move to a job of their own, `tokio-matrices`, which restores the engine and reads the `ci` job's entry as the other feature-set jobs do. The class budgets already sum to 8,465 of the 8,500 MB target, so the new job adds no cache class. `isolated-crates` keeps C3, C1m, C1n and C1ns. Each job is now sized to fit its limit cold, which is the state the pruner can leave it in.

Round 4470.decision_summary: A consumer asked for the consolidation mode of a Query and a Reply as a word. The dissection gave only the byte, so a reader that wanted to show the mode had to carry the byte-to-mode table itself, and that table is a fact of the protocol, so the decoder's. Both walkers now add a `consolidation_name` label beside the `consolidation` byte, which stays. The words are zenoh's `ConsolidationMode` variants on zenoh's numbering (0 Auto, 1 None, 2 Monotonic, 3 Latest), spelled once in `ConsolidationMode::wire_word` in `query_mode.rs`, next to the `wire_byte` numbering an earlier round measured against a real zenohd. A byte zenoh's decoder does not number gets no word; that decoder falls back to Auto for it, but that is its handling of an unreadable byte, not a mode the sender wrote. The byte is read on one numbering and not per sender, because nothing in the message says which implementation wrote it. A stock zenoh-pico 1.10.2 sender writes its API enum raw, one slot low (None 0, Monotonic 1, Latest 2), so its bytes read here as the mode a zenoh receiver applies to them. The label aliases the byte, so the tiling is unchanged, and no document revision moves: the tree gains a name, and the published-path ledger holds it.

Round 4471.decision_summary: A consumer builds its verify image with no network, after fetching every release input once per host into a cache addressed by SHA-256. The zenoh-c oracle installer was the one input it could not hand over: it fetched the release archive itself, git-cloned the source from GitHub, and the pin held no digest, so nothing said the bytes were upstream's. The pin file now carries one `ZENOH_C_SHA256_<target>` per standalone archive upstream publishes for the pinned version, and `ZENOH_C_SOURCE_URL` with `ZENOH_C_SOURCE_SHA256` for the tag's source tarball. The installer takes `WZ_ZENOH_C_ARCHIVE` (the release zip) and `WZ_ZENOH_C_SOURCE` (the tarball, or a directory holding the tree, which is copied and never written to), fetches whichever is unset, and checks every archive against the pinned digest before unpacking it, handed in or fetched, because both are the same claim that the bytes are the release. A target with no digest is refused, and a version override must bring its own digest (`WZ_ZENOH_C_SHA256`, `WZ_ZENOH_C_SOURCE_SHA256`), so no path unpacks an archive unchecked. The source is now the tarball rather than a clone: the tag's tree is the same (zenoh-c marks nothing export-ignore), nothing downstream needs the history, and only bytes can be held to a digest. A directory has no bytes to hash and is held to the version it states, as a checkout always was. Because the gates that derive the tree's upstreams and their pins read only submodules and `git clone` lines, zenoh-c would have dropped out of them; a pin file's tag-archive source URL is now a third shape, read once by `gate_reason_claims.pin_file_sources` for both the fetched set and the pin.

UPDATE (R3058) -- THE C ABI'S PROVIDER IS THE RUNTIME'S, SO WHAT A PROVIDER DOES WHEN IT IS ASKED FOR CHUNKS IS THE REAL LIBRARY'S; THE ATOM STAYS PARTIAL. CHANGED: the provider is no longer in-process memory with an allocator of this crate's own. The built-in provider is the runtime's pool over a POSIX segment, carved by the allocator upstream's default backend uses, and a provider over a C program's callbacks is an adapter implementing the same backend trait (`crates/wz-capi-c/src/shm.rs` @ `struct ForeignBackend`), so both share one set of allocation semantics. The five allocation spellings take the policies zenoh-c gives them: plain, collecting with the unsafe collection, defragmenting, deallocating with a limit of 100, and blocking. A chunk is a shared buffer with a real holder count: `z_shm_clone` shares the bytes where it copied them, and `z_shm_mut_try_from_immut` recovers a buffer nothing else holds where it always refused; both were found by probing the real library and are pinned by this crate's unit tests, not by a differential. MEASURED against the real library, from one C program compiled once and linked twice (`crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/zenoh_c_shm_provider_allocation_twice_and_diff.rs` @ `fn a_providers_allocation_semantics_are_identical_on_wz_and_libzenohc`): which pools are made and refused (0 and 1000 bytes refused, 4096 and 5000 made), how many chunks of each size a pool holds, that a dropped chunk is served again only after a collection, what each policy reports on a full pool and on a fragmented one, and which aligned requests a default provider refuses. It was written before the move and recorded the differences the move had to close; it is identical on both libraries after it. Four mutations of the C ABI, each restored, each reds it: the plain spelling collecting, the deallocating spelling not deallocating, a layout refusal reported as an allocation failure, and a pool of any size served. FOUND AND CHANGED: upstream's `z_get_shm.c` can no longer run on this ABI, as it cannot on the real library, because it sizes its provider at exactly the payload and the real allocator refuses that. The leg that pinned this on the real library now pins both arms refusing, and the witness that a real zenoh-pico queryable reads an SHM-allocated query payload moved to a program derived from that example with one call changed (the provider's size, 4096 as `z_pub_shm.c` uses), compiled for both arms; they print the same reply. What that witnesses is the bytes and not shared-memory transport: `z_bytes_from_shm` still copies, and a pico peer has no segment to map. Also found: the backend of a provider is released by whichever thread lets go of its last reference, so a C program that drops a provider can see its context deleted a moment later on another thread when providers are created concurrently; the crate's tests that asserted the instant now wait, bounded. The crate's unit tests pass on both arms, and twice in a row on the shared-memory arm after that repair. STILL UNBUILT: the SENDING half, which is `z_bytes_from_shm` keeping the chunk so that `z_put`, `z_publisher_put`, `z_get` and the querier put a descriptor on the wire, and a reply doing the same, which needs a runtime reply path that does not exist; the two symbols `z_open_with_custom_shm_clients` and `z_ref_shm_client_storage_global`; and a census of the divergences this crate names, which this reason does not list. plugin-abi-compat.reason: FOUNDATIONAL: REALIZED R311y492 inside plugin-dynamic-loading, with no separate cfg toggle. R311y256 deprecated this atom ON THE CONDITION that dynamic loading was never built, in its own words: the four exist only to SERVE dynamic loading, so if that is ever built they return with it. Runtime: Send + Sync is load-bearing -- the AP profile genuinely moves spawned tasks across worker threads -- and the MCU bundle's Rc is equally load-bearing, since alloc::sync::Arc needs target_has_atomic="ptr" and ARMv6-M lacks it, so making the bundle Send would wall the MCU session off the targets the Rc exists to reach. Both ends are right; the repair is a !Send pool BESIDE the contract, not a weakened contract. The trait is untouched. (2) The per-iteration sequence had to be extracted (SessionPump::step) before either driver could exist, and storing the FSM engine in a struct means NAMING sce_rust_runtime::Engine -- a dep wz-session-lwip does not carry and should not acquire to spell a return type. The sync run_session still takes the executor pass (nothing else drives the runtime there); session_task must NOT, because a task that pumps the pool currently polling it rebuilds the very inversion this closes. Cost of (3): the pass rotated one position in the sync loop, which is a loop rotation and steady-state identical. UPDATE (R3159-R3169) -- THE TRANSMIT HALF (SECTION 9.1) IS BUILT ON BOTH PROFILES, IN THE FORM THE LINK LENDS THE BUFFER, AND THE MCU RECEIVE SIDE (SECTION 9.2) IS HALF BUILT; THE GRADE STAYS PARTIAL AND THE EARLIER CLAUSES THAT SAY THE TRANSMIT PATH IS UNTOUCHED ARE FALSE. Measured against the code, the session cannot own the outbound buffer: the AP stream driver builds a second framed vector and hands it to its writer task by ownership, a multilink session has one link per pool, and only the link knows what its DMA domain needs in front of the payload. So the LINK LENDS and the session encodes. The seam is four defaulted methods on the link driver (acquire a slot with the headroom the link wants, name its storage, send it, abort it), a lease that is a buffer over the lent slot and gives it back if dropped unsent, and an outbound buffer trait that every encoder writes to, so a heap vector and a fixed slot are the same to the codec. The session's immediate and lowlatency send paths try a lease before the heap encode and fall back to the heap, with the sequence number already minted, when the link lends nothing, has no free slot, the encode overflows the slot, or the frame needs fragmenting; the wire is byte for byte the heap path's, witnessed against it. The reconnect swap seams forward the lend and remember which link lent each slot, so a swap in the middle of an encode sends and aborts on the link that lent it. ON THE AP the stream driver lends a vector with the framing prefix room in front of it, writes the prefix in place and enqueues the filled vector by ownership, and the writer task returns each buffer it has written to a small bounded pool (four buffers of at most 16 KiB) that the next lend draws from: two allocations and a copy per frame become none in steady state, witnessed by six frames through the real writer task leaving one buffer, with the pool read directly because a freed buffer's address is what the allocator hands the next request and so proves nothing. ON THE MCU the transmit chain is cut at all three copies that followed the encoder: the Ethernet MAC seam gains a gather transmit and a completion report, the CYT4BF MAC chains one descriptor per piece with the vendor driver's own protocol (read from its reference source) and reports a frame done only when the controller has finished reading it, the lwIP shim holds a reference on the pbuf chain and hands its pieces to the MAC in place, and the lwIP link driver lends the payload of a transport-layer pbuf so the session encodes straight into the datagram; a real pbuf chain whose payload piece is the caller's own memory reaches the MAC at that address with its reference count read as one. The RECEIVE side of the same MAC is cut at the first two of its three copies: the MAC lends a received frame where the controller wrote it and withholds that buffer from the controller until it is returned, the shim wraps it in a custom pbuf that points at it so lwIP reads it in place, and the buffer goes back to the MAC when lwIP frees the pbuf, which for a fragment parked in reassembly is long after the input call returned; the witness is a real lwIP stack receiving a datagram, an ARP reply and a two-fragment datagram through lent frames, each buffer coming back exactly once. Each layer has a red-first break that turns exactly its tests red, and the C and Rust compile for a Cortex-M target with the real lwIP sources. The footprint the paragraph above left unmeasured was read hosted and was red: the MCU multicast image grew 1456 bytes of ROM (thumbv7m 64172 to 65652) over the buffer seam, for a seam it never uses. A per-symbol diff names it: the payload encoders write through a fallible dyn TxBuf sink, which keeps the codec's error branch after every write, where a vector's push cannot fail and that branch folds away. session-close-ingress.reason: PARTIAL: F=a rail message closes a RUNNING session -- the session FSM's `session.close` reachable from outside the process through the one ingress port AP and MCU share. P=no upstream counterpart: zenoh's admin write plane carries no close verb, and its handler could not answer one if it did -- it is a Push primitive at `zenoh/src/net/runtime/adminspace.rs` @ `fn send_push_consume(` with no response channel at all, which is why this verb has no reply and success is observable only as the effect. Catalog precedent for a capability upstream lacks: `switchboard`, `ext-pubsub-group-membership`, `locator-iface`. C=wz opens and closes over the rail; opening already worked (`connect-add` reconciles to a dial and InitSyn leaves, witness `wz_router_hat_connect_reconcile.rs`) and closing now does too. BUILT R2678, and the base it fixes is the reason it took a round to find: THE KEYEXPR MATCHER AND THE FSM ENGINE ARE IN TWO OWNERSHIP DOMAINS THAT WERE NEVER IN SCOPE TOGETHER. The matcher runs under the observer lock on the `Session` handle, whose `SessionInner` does not hold the engine; the engine is owned by `OpenedSession`, moved into `drive_session_until_terminal` and borrowed `&mut` there for its whole life. So the seam is a take-once REQUEST that crosses between them as data: `SessionCore::requested_close` on the shared bundle, `SessionLinkActions::request_close` / `take_requested_close` (the shape `take_pending_batch` already established), and `drive::check_requested_close`, which raises `SessionFsmUnicastEvent::SessionClose` on the engine it is handed -- the peer of `check_lease_deadline`, the only other production raiser in the tree, beside it in the same file and generic over `R: SessionRuntime` for the same reason. THE HOOK WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED: the drive loop calls `on_event(IterationEvent)` while holding the engine, so lending it there was the obvious move and is wrong -- that hook is the application observer fan, and handing every app callback `&mut` on the session's state machine is authority the hook has no business granting. The request travels; the authority stays. INGRESS: `drive::SessionLifecycleInjector` implements the unconditional `EventInjector` port, so the keyexpr table, the matcher and the port are the ones both profiles already share; it is the first injector in the tree that does not wrap an SCE `Engine`. It carries NO literal event name -- it asks the generated machine through `StatePolicy::get_event_from_name`, because a name agreed by hand between two places stays agreed only until one is edited, which is open-debt item 777's whole subject. AP/MCU PARITY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CLAIMED: every piece above is in `wz-session-core`, which both runtimes build, and both forward the feature; nothing was added to the AP-only admin plane, which is `#[cfg(feature = "adminspace-core")]` and alloc-based and which no MCU crate references. WITNESS `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_close_ingress.rs`: a row is registered, a wire Push arrives on it, the ingress stages, the comparator drains, and the assertion is the STATE -- Established to Closing -- because an assertion on the request alone would pass with the raiser deleted. It asserts the ingress did NOT move the machine (it has no engine), that the drain is take-once, and it carries an anti-vacuity arm on an unmapped keyexpr plus a pin that the registered name is the one the document declares. RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: no production host registers a row yet -- the capability is reachable and witnessed end to end, but which keyexpr a deployment exposes it on is a deployment's choice and wz ships no default row, so a node does not answer this verb until its host maps one. AND A LANE RUNS THAT WITNESS, which is a separate sentence from "the witness exists" and the one this grade actually needs: both features are non-default, so the changed-crate push gate compiles the file to NOTHING and no hosted lane turned either on -- the tests would have passed by hand and been executed by nothing, a green over a population of zero. R2678 adds the `wz-runtime-tokio|hook|session-close-ingress,switchboard|session_close_ingress` row to `scripts/lib/nondefault-tests-gate.sh`, so the hook runs them on every push and Layer C1bn runs them hosted. Every test in the file carries the atom's name as a prefix so a test added later is covered without touching that row. REGRADE (Round 2697, owner instruction 2026-09-17, sequencing ruled 2026-09-18): THIS ATOM IS PARTIAL AGAIN, AND THE NUMBER WENT UP. Nothing above was withdrawn -- the machine Round 2678 built still stands and its witnesses still pass. What changed is the SCOPE: the owner's interface decision (open-debt item 761, taken 2026-09-17 under "ignore the cost, be right for the long run") settles three things this grade was never given for, so the honest move is to lower the grade rather than let a COMPLETE keep asserting a scope it does not cover. THE THREE RESIDUALS, in the order the item fixes as the order of work: (a) ACL FIRST -- a lifecycle verb sits behind access control, and the measurement behind that ordering is that `switchboard.rs` and `observer.rs` carry ZERO ACL references while `access-acl` is itself PARTIAL; a destructive verb shipped without its gate cannot be recalled, and adding the gate after a harness starts speaking the verb breaks the harness. Acceptance: a refused command changes nothing, and the refusal is observed as nothing happening, because this port answers nothing by design. (b) ONE DECLARATION -- a second binding kind (`lifecycle:`) in `wz-switchboard.yaml`, so the AP registry and the MCU's generated static match take their row from the SAME document. Today each host wires its own keyexpr by hand, which is the defect class this feature's own comment cites (item 777: a hand-agreed string is agreed only until one side is edited). Acceptance: no host binds a row by hand -- one declaration, two profiles. (c) `open` ON THE SAME DOOR -- the same port and the same grammar, `@/<zid>/<whatami>/session/<verb>/<peer-zid>`, with `connect-add` kept as the AP alias. The exchange: InitSyn carries the initiator's AUTH SEGMENT id; the acceptor MAPS that segment, reads the random challenge inside it, and returns it on InitAck beside its own segment id; the initiator validates the echo against its own challenge, maps the acceptor's segment, and answers with ITS challenge on OpenSyn; the acceptor validates that second echo and confirms with the literal 1 on OpenAck. Each side therefore PROVES map-ability to the other -- a token exchange would pass between two hosts that share nothing. The segment is a real POSIX object (`wz-runtime-tokio::shm_auth_segment`, `/dev/shm/{id}.zenoh` -- the NAME is wire format, since a foreign peer opens exactly that string) holding a u64 array `[protocols.len(), !challenge, SHM_VERSION, POSIX_PROTOCOL_ID]`; the challenge is stored BITWISE-INVERTED as upstream stores it, which is load-bearing interop rather than obfuscation. `SHM_VERSION` mismatch, an unmappable segment, and a wrong echo all degrade to "no shared memory" with the session intact; only a MALFORMED InitSyn body aborts, mirroring zenoh's one `bail!` and its asymmetry with the initiator's tolerant `recv_init_ack`. OPT-IN: the dispatch is EMPTY until an authenticator is installed, and an empty one emits nothing, so a deploy that installs none keeps the pre-R311y507 UNIT wire byte-identical; the two mechanisms never half-mix, because the challenge REPLACES the UNIT ext at the stage seam and the offer predicate follows whichever mechanism is running. THE CONTROL: the same publisher against a wz acceptor that does not offer SHM delivers three raw samples byte-exact, so the zero is about shared memory and not about the topology, the declarations or the harness. wz to zenoh: `z_sub_shm` listens, wz dials, negotiates and calls `publish_shm`; zenoh's RX task fails with `decoding error` (`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/universal/rx.rs` @ `.map_err(|_| zerror!("{}: decoding error", link.link))?;`) and CLOSES THE TRANSPORT.

WHY. With the Put's `ext_shm` marker set, zenoh lays the payload out SLICED (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/zenoh/put.rs` @ `let codec = Zenoh080Sliced::<u32>::new(ext_shm.is_some());`): a count of slices, then per slice a kind byte (RAW 0, SHM_PTR 1) and a length-prefixed body, which for SHM_PTR is the encoded `ShmBufInfo` (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/core/zbuf.rs` @ `impl<W> WCodec<&ZBuf, &mut W> for Zenoh080Sliced<$bound>`). wz writes and reads a single length and the four descriptor varints (`crates/wz-session-core/src/push_build.rs` @ `let payload_len = descriptor_bytes.len() as u64;`). The layout needs the Put codec to branch on a preceding TLV-chain entry, which SCE's `sce:present-if` cannot express: open-debt item 823, reported to SCE on 2026-09-26 and re-measured against SCE's HEAD on 2026-10-01, where it is still refused. A hand-written Put decoder is the wrong repair, because it breaks the codec SSOT, so nothing is built on top of one.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THE RESIDUAL. The order of what can be measured is the layout first (SCE), then, ON TOP OF IT, the lifecycle this reason names, and the same harness already shows which is the next red. `ShmBackedPayload` invalidates its slot and unlinks its segment the moment its owner lets go; zenoh's sender holds the buffer by a reference count it takes on every serialization (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/core/zbuf.rs` @ `unsafe { shmb.inc_ref_count() };`) and the receiver's `Drop` releases it. UPDATE (R3038) -- THE PROVIDER'S LIFECYCLE ARM IS BUILT: A CHUNK NOW LIVES BY UPSTREAM'S REFERENCE COUNT, AND THE ARM THAT WAS A PIN IS THE POSITIVE WITNESS. THE ATOM STAYS PARTIAL ON WHAT IS STILL OPEN. THE DEFECT, AND A SECOND ONE FOUND ON THE WAY. wz's provider invalidated a slot and unlinked its data segment when its owner let go (open-debt item 823 (6)), so a publisher that dropped its payload as `publish_shm` returned left a zenoh reader nothing to open. The second defect was on the receiving side and nothing had measured it: a descriptor is sent with one reference taken for its receiver, and wz's resolver read the chunk and never gave that reference back, so a sustained zenoh shared-memory stream into a wz subscriber would have kept every chunk out of the publisher's pool. MEASURED, with the resolver's release removed, which is what the old resolver did: all three chunks a `z_pub_shm` handed over still read a count of one in zenoh's own metadata segment after wz had read them. THE PROTOCOL, taken from upstream and stated once in the provider's module docs: the count starts at 1 as the owner's own reference; serializing a descriptor takes one more for the receiver (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/core/zbuf.rs` @ `unsafe { shmb.inc_ref_count() };`) and a read takes none; every holder gives its reference back when it lets go (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/lib.rs` @ `impl Drop for ShmBufInner {`); the provider collects a chunk when the count reads zero (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/api/provider/shm_provider.rs` @ `fn garbage_collect_impl<const SAFE: bool>(&self) -> usize {`) and a reclaimed slot advances its generation, which turns every descriptor of it stale (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/metadata/storage.rs` @ `pub fn reclaim(`). WHAT WAS BUILT. Serializing the descriptor is one guarded step: (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `pub fn wire_reference(&self) -> WireReference<'_> {`) takes the reference and returns it if the frame does not build or the send refuses. The resolver gives back the one reference exactly once on every way out once the header's generation shows it is its own, saturating at zero so a replayed descriptor cannot wrap the count; a header of another generation is another buffer's and is not touched, which upstream's reader would decrement. The owner's drop gives back its own reference and parks the data segment, mapped and locked, on a busy list, because upstream's orphan cleanup deletes any segment nobody holds a shared lock on; the list is collected when an owner drops and when a payload is allocated (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `fn collect_garbage(&mut self) -> usize {`), slots go to the back of a first-in first-out queue as upstream's do, and the generation advances at reclaim and not at allocation. The receiver maps the provider's metadata segment WRITABLE, which releasing a reference needs; the first build mapped it read-only and died with a SIGSEGV on the first release. A resolver is now offered EVERY shared-memory slice of a message, not only those before the first fault, because a slice it never sees is a reference nobody releases (`crates/wz-session-core/src/put_payload.rs` @ `fn every_shm_slice_reaches_the_resolver_after_one_fails() {`). WITNESSED, in both directions and off the OTHER side's bookkeeping. Against upstream's own programs, the zenoh-to-wz leg reads zenoh's metadata segment after wz has read each sample and asserts every chunk was given back; the two wz-to-zenoh legs assert the chunk comes home to wz's provider after zenoh's subscriber lets go, a decrement made by zenoh's own drop in a process wz does not control; and the leg for a publisher that lets go at once is the positive twin of the held leg (`crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_shm_payload_zenohd_interop.rs` @ `async fn wz_shm_payload_its_owner_let_go_of_at_once_is_still_readable_by_a_zenohd_shm_subscriber() {`), where it was a pin of the defect. In-process, twelve provider tests, among them the arm that leaves a chunk standing for a receiver after its owner has gone (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `fn an_owner_that_lets_go_leaves_its_chunk_standing_for_the_receiver_that_holds_it() {`). Four mutations, each restored byte for byte: the receiver without its release reds the zenoh-to-wz leg alone, with the count zenoh reports; serializing without the reference reds the let-go leg alone, with the very `Error receiving SHM buffer` the pin used to assert; the owner's drop without its own release reds both wz-to-zenoh legs on the chunk never coming home; the early return in the slice walk reds its test alone. THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. The Open exchange keeps the peer's segment with its challenge and, once the echo of our challenge checks out, opens a handoff from the counter block the peer named, the initiator's OpenSyn for an acceptor and the acceptor's OpenAck for an initiator; a new establishment withdraws it, so a registry never writes the counters of a peer it has left.
